title: Customer security reviews: can you answer fast without promising more than you do?
short: Answer every questionnaire from one dated evidence pack within five working days, and mark planned controls as planned.
answer: This quarter, build one dated evidence pack and one answer library in a standard format such as the CSA CAIQ, and let nothing go out without security's approval. Answer only what is true today, mark planned controls with a date, and accept the clauses NIS2, DORA and the GDPR require while you negotiate how they work.
audience: Sales, security, legal and IT leads at companies that sell to other businesses, especially to EU customers under NIS2 or DORA

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Build one evidence pack.
items.text: Keep your certificate and its scope, the latest audit report, a pentest summary, key policies, the sub-processor list and a monitored incident contact in one dated folder. NIS2's implementing rules accept either a right to audit or a right to receive audit reports[^nis2ir].

items.title: Answer from one library in a standard format.
items.text: Fill in the CSA CAIQ v4.1 once and map every customer form to it. ENISA names the CAIQ and the Shared Assessments SIG as evidence customers can weigh when they choose suppliers[^enisatig].

items.title: Answer only what is true today.
items.text: Mark each control as in place, partly in place or planned with a date, and correct a wrong answer as soon as you find it. In the US, MORSECORP paid $4.6 million after reporting a security score of 104 on a scale up to 110, learning it was really -142 and correcting it only after a subpoena[^morse].

items.title: Offer your own security terms first.
items.text: Write a standard security addendum with your incident notice time, audit approach, sub-processor notice and data locations. Send it with the first questionnaire, so negotiation starts from terms you can keep.

items.title: Let security approve every answer.
items.text: Sales owns the deadline, security owns the content and legal owns anything that becomes a contract term. Send nothing without a named approver and a date.

items.title: Which law drives the request?
items.text: NIS2 makes customers weigh their suppliers' product quality and security practices, including secure development[^nis2]. DORA and the CRA add their own duties. The driver decides which clauses you must accept.

items.title: Does the pack already answer it?
items.text: Send the pack and your CAIQ first and answer only what they leave open. Ask whether the customer accepts them in place of its own form.

items.title: Which product, entity and sites?
items.text: Answer for exactly what the customer buys, and say where an answer differs for other products, regions or subcontractors.

items.title: Does any answer need a decision?
items.text: Send every no, partial or new answer to security, and every promise word, such as all, always or within, to legal.

items.title: What did you send, and when?
items.text: Keep the form, the answers, the date and the approver. If a fact changes, tell the customer before its next review.

blocks.title: What goes in the evidence pack
items: **Certificate and scope.** ISO/IEC 27001, TISAX or C5, with a scope that covers what you sell; see the ISMS sheet. The BSI says no general certificate proves NIS2 compliance[^bsifaq], so expect follow-up questions.

**A report that tests operation.** A SOC 2 or C5 Type 2 report tests whether controls worked over a period, Type 1 only their design[^c5faq]. DORA customers may rely on reports only if they test key controls in operation[^rtscontract]. Add a SOC 3, which can be freely distributed[^soc3].
**Pentest summary.** Date, scope, tester and the fix status of critical and high findings, not the full report; see the penetration testing sheet.

**Product security.** Support period, update policy and a component list. NIS2's implementing rules make cloud and managed service customers ask for lifetime security updates and a description of components[^nis2ir].
**Sub-processor list.** Name, service, country and a way to subscribe to changes. Processors must announce intended changes and give controllers the chance to object[^gdpr].

**Contacts and company data.** A monitored security mailbox and phone line, your legal entity, LEI, ultimate parent and the countries you serve from and store data in. DORA registers need each supplier's LEI or EUID, and an LEI for suppliers outside the EU[^roi].

blocks.title: Standard formats and their terms
items: **CSA CAIQ v4.1.** 283 questions on the Cloud Controls Matrix, released in January 2026[^caiqtime]. To publish it in the STAR Registry, use the STAR Level 1 version; the copy in the CCM download can't be submitted[^ccm41].

**The CAIQ license.** CSA's free versions are for internal reference; changing the CCM, building derivatives or commercial use need a license[^csalic]. Filling in the CAIQ and publishing it in the public STAR Registry is CSA's own route[^star]; don't rebuild it into your own form or product.
**SIG and SIG Lite.** If a customer sends Shared Assessments' SIG, answer it from the same library and keep a copy of what you sent.
**Trust page.** Certificates, SOC 3, sub-processors, the security contact and a request form for NDA documents. ENISA points customers to suppliers that publish their security commitments[^enisatig].
**The customer's own form.** Answer it, but point each answer to your CAIQ or report instead of writing new text.

blocks.title: Contract clauses: accept, negotiate or push back

columns.title: Accept: the law requires them
items: **Audits for processors.** You must allow and contribute to audits, including inspections, by the controller or an auditor it mandates[^gdpr].
**NIS2 flow-down.** Security requirements, incident notice without undue delay, vulnerability handling, audits or audit reports, subcontractor rules and data return at exit[^nis2ir].

**DORA terms.** Data locations with advance notice of changes, incident help at no extra or a preset cost, cooperation with supervisors and exit support. For critical or important functions, also unrestricted audit and access rights and joining threat-led tests[^dora].

columns.title: Negotiate the details
items: **Incident notice.** Agree the trigger, such as a confirmed incident affecting the customer, a time, such as 24 hours, and the updates after it. The EU security laws sheet has the customer's own clocks.

**Audit form.** Offer reports first, then remote or pooled audits. DORA allows pooled audits[^rtscontract] and alternative assurance where other clients' rights are affected[^dora]; GDPR audit fees must not be so high that they deter audits[^edpb0720].
**Sub-processor changes.** A notice period and a right to object, not approval of each change. DORA requires a reasonable notice period for material changes behind critical functions[^rtssub].
**Data location.** Commit to countries, including where support staff access data from. DORA registers record both storage and processing countries[^roi].

columns.title: Push back
items: **Unlimited liability.** Ask legal to cap it and match it to your cover; see the cyber insurance sheet.
**Your policy, as amended.** Accept a dated annex; you can't comply with changes you haven't seen.
**Notice of every suspected event within an hour.** Offer fast notice of confirmed incidents and an open line while you investigate.
**Tests of your shared systems.** Offer your pentest summary and let the customer test its own tenant under your rules.
**Audits on demand.** Outside DORA, offer one a year with 30 days' notice, plus one after a serious incident or at a regulator's request.

blocks.title: On-site audits and right-to-audit requests
items: **Agree the scope in writing.** Dates, auditors, agenda, evidence list and confidentiality. Under the GDPR you may suggest an auditor, but the controller decides[^edpb0720].
**Offer remote first.** The EDPB expects both sides to decide in good faith whether an on-site visit is needed, weighing security concerns, with the final choice left to the controller[^edpb0720].
**Protect other customers.** Show evidence on screen, escort visitors and keep other customers' data, keys and full pentest reports out of reach.
**Pool requests.** When several financial customers ask, propose a pooled audit; DORA's rules allow it[^rtscontract].
**Close findings like your own.** Give each an owner and a date, and send the customer a closure note.

blocks.title: Keep answers current
items: **Date every answer.** Show when it was last reviewed. Review the library every quarter and after a major change, incident or audit.
**Track expiry dates.** Certificates, report periods, pentest dates and insurance. DORA customers must check that reports aren't obsolete[^rtscontract].

**Announce changes before they happen.** A dropped control, a new sub-processor or a new data location. Under DORA, going ahead with a subcontracting change the customer objected to lets it terminate[^rtssub].
**Keep a commitments register.** List every security promise in signed contracts, with an owner and a due date.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Germany's NIS2 law took effect on 6 December 2025.** About 29,500 companies have new security duties[^bsifaq] and must make their suppliers meet suitable security requirements, though the BSIG doesn't oblige suppliers directly[^bsilk].
**CAIQ v4.1 replaced v4.0.** STAR accepts both until December 2027[^caiqtime]. Build new answers on v4.1.
**C5:2026 is final.** Published at the end of March 2026[^c5], it applies to attestations from 1 June 2027, and reports dated or ending from 28 February 2027 must describe planned changes[^c5faq].

**CRA duties reach suppliers.** Since 11 September 2026, manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and inform impacted users, and from December 2027 they must exercise due diligence on components they buy[^cra]. Expect questions on your vulnerability handling; see the supply chain sheet.

**AI questions arrive.** CSA's AI Controls Matrix v1.1 of June 2026 comes with an AI-CAIQ for STAR for AI[^aicm], and the AICPA's October 2026 proposal adds AI governance and model monitoring to SOC 2[^tsc2027]. List which AI services touch customer data.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A new answer set for each customer.** Keep one library and map each form to it.
**Certificates nobody asks for.** Get the one your key customers name; see the ISMS sheet.
**Waiting for an EU cyber posture certificate.** The Commission proposed one in January 2026 to show NIS2 compliance[^ecqa], but it isn't law yet.
**Full pentest reports for every prospect.** A summary answers the question without handing out a map of your weaknesses.
**Questionnaire software before the library.** A dated folder and a spreadsheet of approved answers carry you through the first year.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Saying yes to close the deal.** In the US, the FTC barred GoDaddy from misrepresenting its security after it advertised award-winning security without standard protections such as MFA[^ftcgd]. In Germany, a customer who signed because of a deliberately false answer can rescind the contract[^bgb].
**Answering for the wrong scope.** A certificate for headquarters doesn't cover a hosted service run by another entity.
**Notice times nobody can meet.** A two-hour clock with no one on call breaks the contract on the first weekend.
**Letting a tool or a template answer.** Generated or copied answers describe controls you don't run. Check each against evidence.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Fill in the CAIQ v4.1 once and keep it with a dated evidence folder.
Use a CyberRisikoCheck under DIN SPEC 27076 as a starting point, but not as NIS2 proof[^bsilk].
Name one person who approves answers and one who signs contracts.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Publish a trust page with an NDA request form and a sub-processor change feed.
Agree a standard security addendum and fallback positions with legal.
Get ISO 27001 or a SOC 2 Type 2 report if key customers ask; see the ISMS sheet.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Keep a DORA data sheet with your LEI, parent, countries and subcontractors[^roi].
Offer pooled audits to financial customers[^rtscontract] and plan your first C5:2026 report[^c5faq].
Run requests through one queue with an answer library, owners and expiry dates.
